# @farmfe/js-plugin-less

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-less.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-less
Support `less` for Farm.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-less less</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-less less</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-less less</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage
```ts {2,6}
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginLess from '@farmfe/js-plugin-less';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginLess({ /* options */ })
  ]
}
```

## Options
```ts
export type LessPluginOptions = {
  lessOptions?: Less.Options;
  implementation?: string;
  filters?: {
    resolvedPaths?: string[];
    moduleTypes?: string[];
  };
  additionalData?:
    | string
    | ((context?: string, resolvePath?: string) => string | Promise<string>);
};
```

### lessOptions
Less options. See [less options](https://lesscss.org/usage/#less-options).

Example:
```ts
import path from 'node:path';
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginLess from '@farmfe/js-plugin-less';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginLess({
      lessOptions: {
        paths: [path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'styles')]
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### filters
Which files should be processed by `less`. default to `{ resolvedPaths: ['\\.less$'] }` for load and `{ moduleTypes: ['less'] }` for transform.

* `resolvedPaths`: Only files under these paths will be processed. Support regex.
* `moduleTypes`: Only files with these module types will be processed.

`resolvedPaths` and `moduleTypes` are unioned, which means files match any of them will be processed.

Example:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginLess from '@farmfe/js-plugin-less';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginLess({
      filters: {
        // all files end with .custom-css will be processed
        resolvedPaths: ['\\.custom-less$'],
        moduleTypes: ['less']
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### implementation
`implementation` package name of `less`. Default to `less`.

### additionalData
```ts
type AdditionalDataOption = string | ((content?: string, resolvePath?: string) => string | Promise<string>);
```
Additional data to be added to every less file. Example:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginLess from '@farmfe/js-plugin-less';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginLess({
      // add variables.less to every less file
      additionalData: `
        @import "./src/styles/variables.less";
      `
    })
  ]
}
```
For less file:
```less title="index.less"
.foo {
  color: @primary-color;
}
```
`additionalData` will be added to the top of the file:
```less title="index.less"
@import "./src/styles/variables.less";

.foo {
  color: @primary-color;
}
```

Function form:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginLess from '@farmfe/js-plugin-less';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginLess({
      // add variables.less to every less file
      additionalData: (content, resolvePath) => {
        if (resolvePath === '/path/to/index.less') {
          return `
            @import "./src/styles/variables.less";
          `;
        }
      }
    })
  ]
}
```

---

# @farmfe/js-plugin-postcss

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-postcss.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-postcss
Support `postcss` for Farm.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-postcss postcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-postcss postcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-postcss postcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage
```ts {2,6}
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginPostcss from '@farmfe/js-plugin-postcss';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginPostcss({ /* options */ })
  ]
}
```

## Options
```ts
export type PostcssPluginOptions = {
  /**
   * @default undefined
   * postcss-load-config options. path default to farm.config.js root.
   */
  postcssLoadConfig?: {
    ctx?: postcssLoadConfig.ConfigContext;
    path?: string;
    options?: Parameters<typeof postcssLoadConfig>[2];
  };
  filters?: {
    resolvedPaths?: string[];
    moduleTypes?: string[];
  };
  implementation?: string;
};

```

### postcssLoadConfig
Farm uses `postcss-load-config` to load `postcss` config, so you can use `postcss-load-config`'s options. Refer to [postcss-load-config](https://github.com/postcss/postcss-load-config).

Example:
```ts
import path from 'node:path';
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginPostcss from '@farmfe/js-plugin-postcss';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginPostcss({
      postcssLoadConfig: {
        // load config from client/postcss.config.js
        path: path.join(process.cwd(), 'client')
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### filters
Which files should be processed by `postcss`. default to `{ moduleTypes: ['css'] }`.

* `resolvedPaths`: Only files under these paths will be processed. Support regex.
* `moduleTypes`: Only files with these module types will be processed. note that less/sass files should be processed by `@farmfe/js-plugin-less`/`@farmfe/plugin-sass` first. 

`resolvedPaths` and `moduleTypes` are unioned, which means files match any of them will be processed.

Example:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginPostcss from '@farmfe/js-plugin-postcss';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginPostcss({
      filters: {
        // all files end with .custom-css will be processed
        resolvedPaths: ['\\.custom-css$'],
        moduleTypes: ['css']
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### implementation
`implementation` package name of `postcss`. Default to `postcss`.

---

# @farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-qiankun.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun

JavaScript plugin for exposing Farm applications as qiankun micro-apps.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun --dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the HTML transform plugin:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import { qiankunFarmPlugin } from "@farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    qiankunFarmPlugin({
      appName: "myMicroApp",
      devMode: true,
    }),
  ],
});
```

Then register lifecycle hooks in your app entry:

```ts
import { injectQiankun } from "@farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun/helper";

injectQiankun({
  async bootstrap() {},
  async mount(props) {
    console.log(props);
  },
  async unmount() {},
});
```

## Options

### Plugin options

- `appName: string` — required qiankun app name. It must be a valid JavaScript identifier; the plugin throws otherwise.
- `devMode?: boolean` — append debug logging to the injected helper script. Defaults to `false`.

### `injectQiankun` options

- `bootstrap: () => Promise<void>`
- `mount: (props: unknown) => Promise<void>`
- `unmount: () => Promise<void>`
- `update?: (props: unknown) => Promise<void>`

The Farm plugin appends a script to the HTML body that bridges these helper hooks to `window[appName]`.

---

# @farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-react-compiler.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler

JavaScript plugin that runs React Compiler through Babel for matched JSX/TSX modules.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler --dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import react from "@farmfe/plugin-react";
import { reactCompiler } from "@farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    reactCompiler(),
    react(),
  ],
});
```

## Options

- `filters?: { moduleTypes?: ModuleType[]; resolvedPaths?: string[] }` — modules to transform. Defaults to module types `["jsx", "tsx"]` and no path filters.
The generated Farm plugin is named `"js-plugin:react-compiler"` and uses priority `120`.

:::note
The current implementation always configures Babel with `babel-plugin-react-compiler` and `@babel/plugin-syntax-jsx`.
:::

# @farmfe/js-plugin-sass

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-sass.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-sass
Support `sass` for Farm.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-sass sass</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-sass sass</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-sass sass</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage
```ts {2,6}
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({ /* options */ })
  ]
}
```

## Options
```ts
export type SassPluginOptions = {
  sassOptions?: StringOptions<'async'>;
  filters?: {
    resolvedPaths?: string[];
    moduleTypes?: string[];
  };

  /**
   * - relative or absolute path
   * - globals file will be added to the top of the sass file
   * - when file changed, the file can't be hot-reloaded
   *
   * relative to project root or cwd
   */
  implementation?: string | undefined;
  globals?: string[];
  additionalData?:
    | string
    | ((content?: string, resolvePath?: string) => string | Promise<string>);
};
```

### sassOptions
Sass options. See [sass options](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/interfaces/options/) for more details.

Example:
```ts
import path from 'node:path';
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({
      sassOptions: {
        loadPaths: [path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'styles')]
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### filters
Which files should be processed by `sass`. Default to `{ resolvedPaths: ['\\.(s[ac]ss)$'] }` for load and `{ moduleTypes: ['sass'] }` for transform.

* `resolvedPaths`: Only files under these paths will be processed. Support regex.
* `moduleTypes`: Only files with these module types will be processed.

`resolvedPaths` and `moduleTypes` are unioned, which means files match any of them will be processed.

Example:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({
      filters: {
        // all files end with .custom-css will be processed
        resolvedPaths: ['\\.custom-sass$'],
        moduleTypes: ['sass']
      }
    })
  ]
}

export default config;
```

### implementation
`implementation` package name of `sass`. Default to `sass`. If you want to use `sass-embedded`, you can set it to `sass-embedded`.

```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({
      implementation: 'sass-embedded'
    })
  ]
}
```
:::note
You should install `sass-embedded` manually.
:::

### additionalData
```ts
type AdditionalDataOption = string | ((content?: string, resolvePath?: string) => string | Promise<string>);
```
Additional data to be added to every sass file. Example:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({
      // add variables.sass to every sass file
      additionalData: `
        @import "./src/styles/variables.scss";
      `
    })
  ]
}
```
For sass file:
```sass title="index.scss"
.foo {
  color: @primary-color;
}
```
`additionalData` will be added to the top of the file:
```sass title="index.scss"
@import "./src/styles/variables.scss";

.foo {
  color: @primary-color;
}
```

Function form:
```ts
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import farmJsPluginSass from '@farmfe/js-plugin-sass';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    farmJsPluginSass({
      // add variables.sass to every sass file
      additionalData: (content, resolvePath) => {
        if (resolvePath === '/path/to/index.sass') {
          return `
            @import "./src/styles/variables.sass";
          `;
        }
      }
    })
  ]
}
```

### globals
Global sass files. These files will be added to the top of every sass file. It's the same as `additionalData` but more convenient.


---

# @farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-tailwindcss.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss

TailwindCSS integration for Farm using the official TailwindCSS Node and Oxide packages. This is the JavaScript-plugin alternative to the Rust [`@farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss`](./tailwindcss) package.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

```ts {2,6}
import { defineConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import tailwindcss from '@farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    ...tailwindcss()
  ]
});
```

Then import Tailwind from a CSS entry:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

## Options

```ts
export interface Options {
  filters?: {
    resolvedPaths?: string[];
    moduleTypes?: string[];
  };
}
```

### `filters`

Controls which modules are scanned for TailwindCSS class candidates. By default, the plugin scans transformed project files and excludes `node_modules`.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import tailwindcss from '@farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    ...tailwindcss({
      filters: {
        resolvedPaths: ['src/'],
        moduleTypes: ['tsx', 'jsx', 'html']
      }
    })
  ]
});
```

## How it works

The plugin scans transformed modules with `@tailwindcss/oxide`, stores the candidates in Farm metadata, and generates CSS for CSS root files during `freezeModule` with `@tailwindcss/node`. It also tracks scanned modules as watch files for rebuilds.

Prefer the Rust plugin for the default Farm-native path. Prefer this JS plugin when you need JS plugin filters or want to integrate with the JavaScript Tailwind pipeline directly.

---

# @farmfe/js-plugin-visualizer

# @farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/js-vuetify.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify

JavaScript plugin for Vuetify component/directive auto-imports and Vuetify style resolution.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify vuetify unplugin-vue --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify vuetify unplugin-vue --dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify vuetify unplugin-vue --save-dev</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import vue from "unplugin-vue/vite";
import vuetify from "@farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify";

export default defineConfig({
  vitePlugins: [vue()],
  plugins: [
    vuetify({
      autoImport: true,
      styles: "sass",
    }),
  ],
});
```

The plugin requires a Vue plugin named `unplugin-vue` or `vite:vue` in `vitePlugins`; it throws if none is found.

## Options

Options are based on `@vuetify/loader-shared`.

- `autoImport?: boolean | { labs?: boolean; ignore?: string[] }` — enable Vuetify component and directive imports. Defaults to `true`.
- `styles?: true | "none" | "sass" | { configFile: string }` — control Vuetify style imports. Defaults to `true`.

When `autoImport` is enabled, `.vue` files and Vue template/script virtual modules are scanned for Vuetify imports. The style resolver plugin is only registered when `styles` is `"none"`, `"sass"`, or an object with `configFile`.

The package also re-exports `transformAssetUrls` from `@vuetify/loader-shared`.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-mdx

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/mdx.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-mdx

Rust plugin that loads `.md` and `.mdx` files and compiles them to JSX with `mdxjs`.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-mdx @farmfe/plugin-react</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-mdx @farmfe/plugin-react</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-mdx @farmfe/plugin-react</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import mdx from "@farmfe/plugin-mdx";
import react from "@farmfe/plugin-react";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    mdx({
      include: "\\.(md|mdx)$",
    }),
    react({ runtime: "automatic" }),
  ],
});
```

Then import MDX as a component:

```tsx
import Page from "./page.mdx";

export default () => <Page />;
```

## Options

The Rust implementation accepts MDX compiler options plus Farm filters:

- `include?: string` — regular expression string; when set, only matching resolved paths are transformed.
- `exclude?: string` — regular expression string; matching resolved paths are skipped.
- `development?: boolean` — passed to `mdxjs`. Defaults to `false`.
- `providerImportSource?: string`
- `jsx?: boolean` — defaults to `false`.
- `jsxRuntime?: "automatic" | "classic"` — defaults to `"automatic"`.
- `pragma?: string` — defaults to `"React.createElement"`.
- `pragmaFrag?: string` — defaults to `"React.Fragment"`.
- `pragmaImportSource?: string` — defaults to `"react"`.
- `jsxImportSource?: string` — defaults to `"react"`.
- `filepath?: string`
- `parse?: object` — passed to `mdxjs` parse options.

`jsx` and `jsxRuntime` are passed through to `mdxjs` together: `jsx` controls whether JSX is preserved in the output, while `jsxRuntime` controls the runtime mode used when MDX compiles JSX. If `jsx` is `false`, MDX compiles JSX away using the selected runtime mode.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-modular-import

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/modular-import.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-modular-import

A Rust Farm plugin for transforming named UI-library imports into per-component imports with matching style imports.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install -D @farmfe/plugin-modular-import</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add -D @farmfe/plugin-modular-import</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add -D @farmfe/plugin-modular-import</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import modularImport from "@farmfe/plugin-modular-import";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    modularImport({
      libraryName: "element-ui",
    }),
  ],
});
```

This transforms:

```js
import { SomeComponent } from "element-ui";
```

to:

```js
import SomeComponent from "element-ui/lib/SomeComponent";
import "element-ui/lib/SomeComponent/index.css";
```

## Options

- `libraryName: string` — UI library package name to transform.
- `libDir?: string` — component library directory. Defaults to `"lib"`.
- `camel2Dash?: boolean` — controls component-name casing. Defaults to `true`.
- `styleLibDir?: string` — style library directory. Defaults to `"lib"`.
- `styleLibraryName?: string` — optional style library name, for example `"theme-default"`.
- `styleLibraryPath?: string` — custom style path. Defaults to `"index.css"`.

For example, configuring `libDir`, `styleLibraryName`, and `styleLibraryPath`:

```ts
modularImport({
  libraryName: "element-ui",
  libDir: "es",
  styleLibraryName: "theme-default",
  styleLibraryPath: "style/index.css",
});
```

---

# Overview

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/overview.md

# Overview

Farm officially provides a lot of useful plugins, including Rust plugins and JS plugins. Rust plugins are much faster than Js plugins, we recommend to use Rust plugins whenever possible.

:::tip
Refer to [Using Plugins](/docs/using-plugins) for how to use plugins in Farm.
:::

## Rust Plugins

* **[`@farmfe/plugin-react`](./react)**：Support React `jsx` and `react-refresh`.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-vue`](./vue)**：Compile Vue 3 Single-File Components via the `fervid` Rust compiler.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-sass`](./sass)**：Support compiling `sass/scss` files.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-auto-import`](./auto-import)**：Inject imports from presets and scanned local exports.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss`](./tailwindcss)**：Rust-based TailwindCSS integration.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-svgr`](./svgr)**：Transform SVG files into React components.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-wasm`](./wasm)**：Support WebAssembly and `wasm-pack` generated modules.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-worker`](./worker)**：Support web workers via constructors and worker query suffixes.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-url`](./url)**：Import files as data URIs or emitted asset URLs.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-dts`](./dts)**：Emit `.d.ts` files for matched TypeScript modules.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-icons`](./icons)**：Use Iconify icons as on-demand framework components.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-image`](./image)**：Import image files as base64 data URIs or DOM `Image` exports.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-mdx`](./mdx)**：Compile `.md` and `.mdx` files to JSX.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-compress`](./compress)**：Compress generated assets with Brotli, Gzip, Deflate, or DeflateRaw.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-modular-import`](./modular-import)**：Transform UI-library named imports into per-component imports.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname`](./replace-dirname)**：Replace `__dirname`, `__filename`, and `import.meta.url` in script modules.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-strip`](./strip)**：A Farm rust plugin to remove `debugger` statements and functions like `assert.equal` and `console.log` from your code.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-dsv`](./dsv)**：A Farm plugin which converts `.csv` and `.tsv` files into JavaScript modules.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-yaml`](./yaml)**：A Farm plugin which Converts YAML files to ES6 modules.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-virtual`](./virtual)**：A rust plugin for farm to easily use virtual module.
* **[`@farmfe/plugin-react-components`](./react-components)**：On-demand components auto importing for React.

## Js Plugins

* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-postcss`](./js-postcss)**：Support `postcss` in your project.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-babel`](./js-babel)**：Run Babel on matched Farm modules.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-copy`](./js-copy)**：Copy files and globs at the end of a Farm build.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-less`](./js-less)**：Support compiling `less` files.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-svgr`](./js-svgr)**：Support compiling `svg` files.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-dts`](./js-dts)**：Support compiling `*.d.ts` files.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-sass`](./js-sass)**：Support compiling `sass/scss` files.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss`](./js-tailwindcss)**：Support TailwindCSS integration.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-visualizer`](./js-visualizer)**：Visualize your bundle size and composition.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-electron`](./js-electron)**：Support building Electron applications.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-qiankun`](./js-qiankun)**：Expose Farm apps as qiankun micro-apps.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-react-compiler`](./js-react-compiler)**：Run React Compiler through Babel for JSX/TSX modules.
* **[`@farmfe/js-plugin-vuetify`](./js-vuetify)**：Support Vuetify auto-imports and style resolution.

## Community Plugins

If official plugins doesn't meet your needs, you can try [Community Plugins](../community-plugins)

And of course check out [awesome-farm](https://github.com/farm-fe/awesome-farm) - you can also submit a PR to list your plugins there.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-react-components

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/react-components.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-react-components

On-demand components auto importing for React.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-react-components</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-react-components</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-react-components</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage
Import `@farmfe/plugin-react-components` and call it as a factory function in the `plugins` field of `farm.config.ts`, just like a JS plugin.
```ts {2,5}
import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import reactComponents from '@farmfe/plugin-react-components';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [reactComponents({ /** options here */ })]
}
```

## Features

- 💚 Supports React out-of-the-box.
- ✨ Supports both components and directives.
- 🏝 Tree-shakable, only registers the components you use.
- 🪐 Folder names as namespaces.
- 🦾 Full TypeScript support.
- 🌈 [Built-in resolvers](#importing-from-ui-libraries) for popular UI libraries.

## Usage

Use components in templates as you would usually do, it will import components on demand, and there is no `import` and `component registration` required anymore! If you register the parent component asynchronously (or lazy route), the auto-imported components will be code-split along with their parent.

It will automatically turn this

```tsx
export function Main() {
  return <HelloWorld msg="Hello React + Farm" />
}
```

into this

```tsx
import HelloWorld from './src/components/HelloWorld'

export function Main() {
  return <HelloWorld msg="Hello React + Farm" />
}
```

> **Note**
> By default this plugin will import components in the `src/components` path. You can customize it using the `dirs` option.

## TypeScript

To get TypeScript support for auto-imported components.

```ts
Components({
  dts: true, // enabled by default if `typescript` is installed
})
```

Once the setup is done, a `components.d.ts` will be generated and updates automatically with the type definitions. Feel free to commit it into git or not as you want.

> **Make sure you also add `components.d.ts` to your `tsconfig.json` under `include`.**

## Importing from UI Libraries

We have several built-in resolvers for popular UI libraries like **Ant Design**, **Arco Design**, and **Material UI**, where you can enable them by:

Supported Resolvers:

- [Ant Design](https://ant.design/)
- [Arco Design](https://arco.design/react/docs/start)
- [Material UI](https://mui.com/)

```ts
// farm.config.js

import { UserConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import reactComponents from '@farmfe/plugin-react-components';

const config: UserConfig = {
  plugins: [
    reactComponents({
      local: true,
      resolvers: [
        {
          module: "antd",
          prefix: "Ant"
        },
        {
          module: "@arco-design/web-react",
          prefix: "Arco",
          import_style: true // style/index.js
        }
      ]
    })
  ]
}
```

## Configuration

The following show the default values of the configuration
<strike>component</strike>
```ts
{
  // relative paths to the directory to search for components.
  dirs: ['src/components'],
  
  // resolvers for custom components.
  resolvers: [],

  /**
   * Components are introduced with Absolute or Relative path.
   *
   * @default Absolute
   */
  import_mode: "Absolute"

  /**
   * Is it valid for local components
   *
   * @default true
   */
  local: true,

  /**
   * import style `style/index.js` , also accepts a path for custom path (<Component>/**) with components
   *
   * @default false
   */
  importStyle?: boolean | string 

  // generate `components.d.ts` global declarations,
  // also accepts a path for custom filename
  // default: `true` if package typescript is installed
  dts: true,

  // Filters for transforming targets (components to insert the auto import)
  // Note these are NOT about including/excluding components registered - use `Regex` for that
  include: ["src/components"],
  exclude: ["node_modules"],
}
```

# @farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/replace-dirname.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname

Rust plugin that replaces Node-style path globals in script modules.

It rewrites `__dirname`, `__filename`, and `import.meta.url` to string literals based on the module path.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

`@farmfe/core` uses this plugin internally when bundling Farm config files. To register it manually, import the platform plugin path and pass it as a Rust plugin tuple:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import replaceDirname from "@farmfe/plugin-replace-dirname";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    [replaceDirname, {
      include: ["src/"],
      exclude: ["node_modules/"],
    }],
  ],
});
```

## Options

- `include?: string[]` — regular expression strings for module paths to transform. Defaults to `[]`.
- `exclude?: string[]` — regular expression strings for module paths to skip. Defaults to `["node_modules/"]`.

:::warning
Unlike most Rust plugin packages, this package's default export is the resolved native plugin path string, not an options wrapper function.
:::

# @farmfe/plugin-strip

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/strip.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";


# @farmfe/plugin-strip

🍣 A Farm rust plugin to remove `debugger` statements and functions like `assert.equal` and `console.log` from your code.

## Requirements

This plugin requires an [LTS](https://github.com/nodejs/Release) Node version (v18.0.0+) and Farm v1.0.0+.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-strip</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-strip</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-strip</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Create a `farm.config.js` [configuration file](https://www.farmfe.org/docs/config/configuring-farm) and import the plugin:

```js
import { defineConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import strip from '@farmfe/plugin-strip';

export default defineConfig({
  // ...
  plugins: [
    [
      strip({
        // plugin options
        functions:[ 'console.*', 'assert.*' ],
        labels: ['unittest']
      })
    ]
  ],
  // ...
});
```

## Options

### `include`

Type: `String | RegExp | Array[...String|RegExp]`<br/>
Default: `['**/*.js']`<br/>
Example: `include: '**/*.(mjs|js)',`<br/>

A pattern, or array of patterns, which specify the files in the build the plugin should operate on.

### `exclude`

Type: `String | RegExp | Array[...String|RegExp]`<br/>
Default: `[]`<br/>
Example: `exlude: 'tests/**/*',`<br/>

A pattern, or array of patterns, which specify the files in the build the plugin should _ignore_.

### `debugger`

Type: `Boolean`<br/>
Default: `true`<br/>
Example: `debugger: false,`<br/>

If `true` instructs the plugin to remove debugger statements.

### `functions`

Type: `Array[...String]`<br/>
Default: `[ 'console.*', 'assert.*' ]`<br/>
Example: `functions: [ 'console.log', 'MyClass.Test' ],`<br/>

Specifies the functions that the plugin will target and remove.

_Note: specifying functions that are used at the begining of a chain, such as 'a().b().c()', will result in '(void 0).b().c()' which will generate an error at runtime._

### `labels`

Type: `Array[...String]`<br/>
Default: `[]`<br/>
Example: `labels: ['unittest'],`<br/>

Specifies the [labeled blocks or statements](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/label) that the plugin will target and remove.

_Note: the '**:**' is implied and should not be specified in the config._

### `sourceMap`

Type: `Boolean`<br/>
Default: `true`<br/>
Example: `sourceMap: false,`<br/>

If `true`, instructs the plugin to update source maps accordingly after removing configured targets from the bundle.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-svgr

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/svgr.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-svgr

A Rust Farm plugin that transforms SVG files into React components.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install -D @farmfe/plugin-svgr</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add -D @farmfe/plugin-svgr</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add -D @farmfe/plugin-svgr</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import svgr from "@farmfe/plugin-svgr";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    svgr({
      include: ["src/**/*.svg"],
      exclude: ["src/icons/*.svg"],
      defaultStyle: { fill: "currentColor" },
      defaultClass: "svg-icon",
    }),
  ],
});
```

Then import SVG files as React components:

```jsx
import Logo from "./logo.svg";

export function App() {
  return <Logo width={50} height={50} />;
}
```

## Options

- `include?: string[]` — SVG file patterns to transform. Defaults to `["**/*.svg"]`.
- `exclude?: string[]` — SVG file patterns to skip.
- `defaultClass?: string` — default class name added to the generated SVG.
- `defaultStyle?: object` — default style object added to the generated SVG.

SVG imports with `?raw`, `?url`, `?inline`, or `?img=true` are ignored by this plugin.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/tailwindcss.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss

Rust-based TailwindCSS integration for Farm. It scans Farm modules with Tailwind's Oxide scanner and compiles CSS roots that contain Tailwind directives.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss tailwindcss</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the Rust plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts {5}
import { defineConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import tailwindcss from '@farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    tailwindcss({
      config: {
        theme: {
          extend: {}
        }
      }
    })
  ]
});
```

Then import Tailwind from a CSS entry:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
```

## Options

```ts
export interface TailwindCSSOptions {
  /**
   * Reserved for future explicit file/glob scanning. Current builds scan Farm
   * modules that pass through the compilation graph and exclude node_modules.
   */
  content?: string[];

  /**
   * JSON-serializable TailwindCSS configuration.
   *
   * When omitted, Tailwind's default configuration is used.
   */
  config?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### `content`

`content` is part of the public options shape but is reserved for future explicit file/glob scanning. Current builds scan candidate classes from Farm modules that pass through the compilation graph (`js`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`, `vue`, `svelte`, `html`, and `css`) and skip files under `node_modules`.

### `config`

Pass a JSON-serializable TailwindCSS configuration object. If `config` is omitted, Tailwind's default configuration is used.

:::note
The Rust wrapper serializes options before passing them to the underlying TailwindCSS processor, so pass `config` as plain data instead of a JavaScript config file with functions.
:::

## How it works

The plugin runs in two phases:

1. During `transform`, it scans non-CSS source modules for Tailwind class candidates and records CSS root files that contain `@tailwind`, `@apply`, or `@import "tailwindcss"`.
2. During `freezeModule`, it compiles the recorded CSS root with the complete candidate set, rewrites URLs, and updates the CSS module content.

Use `@farmfe/plugin-tailwindcss` when you want the Rust integration. Use [`@farmfe/js-plugin-tailwindcss`](./js-tailwindcss) when you specifically need the JavaScript plugin pipeline or its filter options.

:::note Known limitations
The current Rust plugin scans modules that Farm compiles; it does not yet expand the `content` option into additional filesystem globs. It also accepts JSON-serializable config objects instead of loading arbitrary JavaScript Tailwind config files.
:::

---

# @farmfe/plugin-url

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/url.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-url

A Rust Farm plugin that imports files as data URIs or emitted asset URLs.

## Requirements

This plugin requires Node.js v18.0.0+ and Farm v1.0.0+.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install -D @farmfe/plugin-url</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add -D @farmfe/plugin-url</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add -D @farmfe/plugin-url</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import url from "@farmfe/plugin-url";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    url({
      limit: 14 * 1024,
    }),
  ],
});
```

Then import matching assets:

```js
import svg from "./image.svg";

console.log(`svg contents: ${svg}`);
```

## Options

- `include?: string[]` — regex patterns for files the plugin should process. Defaults to SVG, PNG, JPG/JPEG, GIF, and WebP.
- `exclude?: string[]` — regex patterns for files the plugin should ignore.
- `limit?: number` — inline files up to this size in bytes. Defaults to `14336` (14 KB). Set `0` to emit all matching files.
- `emitFiles?: boolean` — when `false`, files larger than `limit` are returned as data URIs instead of being emitted. Defaults to `true`.

The package types also declare `publicPath`, `filename`, `sourceDir`, and `destDir`, but the current implementation ignores those fields. Do not include them in user configurations today. Emitted files use Farm's configured `output.publicPath` and the source file's basename.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-virtual

# @farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/vue-jsx.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx

Transform Vue JSX/TSX at build time — converts directives (`v-model`, `v-show`, etc.) into Vue 3 runtime calls. Written in Rust with zero JS overhead.

This plugin is the Farm-native equivalent of `@vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx`, ported from `swc-plugin-vue-jsx`.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import vueJsx from "@farmfe/plugin-vue-jsx";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vueJsx()],
});
```

With options:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vueJsx({
      optimize: true,
      transformOn: true,
      resolveType: true,
    }),
  ],
});
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `transformOn` | `boolean` | `false` | Convert `on` / `nativeOn` attrs via `@vue/babel-helper-vue-transform-on` |
| `optimize` | `boolean` | `false` | Inject Vue PatchFlags for optimized VNode updates |
| `customElementPatterns` | `string[]` | `[]` | Regex patterns for custom element tags |
| `mergeProps` | `boolean` | `true` | Merge attribute objects with Vue's `mergeProps` |
| `enableObjectSlots` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable object slot detection |
| `pragma` | `string` | `undefined` | Custom pragma (e.g. `h`), overrides `createVNode` |
| `resolveType` | `boolean` | `false` | Resolve TypeScript types for `defineComponent` props/emits |

## transformOn

When enabled, `on` and `nativeOn` attributes are converted using `@vue/babel-helper-vue-transform-on`. You must install this package in your project:

```bash
pnpm add @vue/babel-helper-vue-transform-on
```

---

# @farmfe/plugin-vue

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/vue.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-vue

Compile [Vue 3 Single-File Components](https://vuejs.org/guide/scaling-up/sfc.html) using the [`fervid`](https://github.com/phoenix-ru/fervid) Rust compiler.

This plugin is the Farm-native equivalent of [`unplugin-vue`](https://github.com/unplugin/unplugin-vue) / [`@vitejs/plugin-vue`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-vue), but written entirely in Rust — no JavaScript orchestration is required at compile time.

:::caution Experimental
`fervid`'s SFC compiler is still maturing (the upstream README marks the compile entry point as "not production-ready yet"). Expect rough edges on edge cases such as advanced `<script setup>` macros and SSR codegen. Please file issues with reproductions; we'll forward to the upstream as needed.
:::

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-vue vue</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-vue vue</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-vue vue</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

`@farmfe/plugin-vue` is a Rust plugin — import it and call it inside the `plugins` array of your `farm.config.ts`, the same as a JS plugin.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import vue from "@farmfe/plugin-vue";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue({
      // options (see below) — may be omitted entirely
    }),
  ],
});
```

If you don't need any options, simply call it with no arguments:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import vue from "@farmfe/plugin-vue";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vue()],
});
```

## Options

| Option                                       | Type                                                  | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `include`                                    | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]`            | `/\.vue$/`     | Files matched by this filter are treated as Vue SFCs.                                                                                                    |
| `exclude`                                    | `string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]`            | `[]`           | Files excluded from the Vue SFC pipeline.                                                                                                                |
| `isProduction`                               | `boolean`                                             | derived        | Force production-mode codegen regardless of Farm's compilation mode.                                                                                     |
| `ssr`                                        | `boolean`                                             | `false`        | Enable fervid's SSR codegen path. Experimental.                                                                                                          |
| `sourceMap`                                  | `boolean`                                             | `true`         | Request source maps from fervid.                                                                                                                         |
| `customElement`                              | `boolean \| string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]` | deprecated     | Backward-compatible alias; prefer `features.customElement`.                                                                                               |
| `features.optionsAPI`                        | `boolean`                                             | `true`         | Drives the `__VUE_OPTIONS_API__` runtime define flag.                                                                                                    |
| `features.prodDevtools`                      | `boolean`                                             | `false`        | Drives `__VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__`.                                                                                                                          |
| `features.prodHydrationMismatchDetails`      | `boolean`                                             | `false`        | Drives `__VUE_PROD_HYDRATION_MISMATCH_DETAILS__`.                                                                                                        |
| `features.propsDestructure`                  | `boolean`                                             | fervid default | Enable reactive destructure for `defineProps`.                                                                                                           |
| `features.customElement`                     | `boolean \| string \| RegExp \| (string \| RegExp)[]` | `/\.ce\.vue$/` | Files matching this pattern are compiled in custom-element mode.                                                                                         |

### Auto-injected `define` flags

In the `config` hook the plugin populates `compilation.define` with the standard Vue feature flags if you have not set them yourself:

- `__VUE_OPTIONS_API__` &nbsp;→ `true`
- `__VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__` &nbsp;→ `false`
- `__VUE_PROD_HYDRATION_MISMATCH_DETAILS__` &nbsp;→ `false`

`vue` is also added to `resolve.dedupe` (except when the build targets Node).

### Style sub-blocks

Each `<style>` block is exposed as a virtual sub-module with a stable query format:

```
foo.vue?vue&type=style&idx=<N>&lang=<lang>&scoped=<bool>
```

For native CSS the virtual module is emitted as `ModuleType::Css` and handled by Farm's built-in CSS pipeline. For non-CSS languages (`scss`, `sass`, `less`, `stylus`) it is emitted as `ModuleType::Custom("<lang>")` so a downstream preprocessor plugin (e.g. `@farmfe/plugin-sass`) can claim it.

### Custom blocks

Custom SFC blocks are exposed as virtual modules so user plugins can opt into blocks such as `<i18n>` or `<docs>`:

```
foo.vue?vue&type=custom&idx=<N>&block=<tag>&lang=<tag>
```

The module type is `ModuleType::Custom("<tag>")`. If no downstream plugin claims that module type, Farm's normal unknown-module behavior applies.

### HMR and scoped preprocessors

The plugin caches descriptor metadata during transform (source hash, style block metadata, custom block metadata, custom-element mode, and virtual ids). This is the Rust-side foundation for granular HMR, but the current safe fallback is still full SFC invalidation when Farm cannot express a narrower update.

Scoped native CSS is handled by `fervid`. Scoped preprocessed blocks are passed to downstream preprocessors as `ModuleType::Custom("<lang>")`; post-preprocessor re-scoping is still gated on a Farm hook that can run after Sass/Less compilation without moving those preprocessors into plugin-vue.

## Reference example

See `examples/vue/` for a small Vue 3 app using `@farmfe/plugin-vue`, Vue Router, Pinia, scoped CSS, and an SCSS SFC style block.

## Feature support (Phase 2)

The plugin intentionally covers the `fervid`-backed subset of `unplugin-vue`; features that require upstream compiler support are gated instead of being silently emulated.

| Capability                                                | Status |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `.vue` load + main module transform                       | ✅      |
| `<script setup>` / Options API                            | ✅      |
| Scoped CSS for native `<style>` blocks                    | ✅      |
| `v-bind(var)` CSS variables (native CSS)                  | ✅      |
| Custom elements via `.ce.vue` or `features.customElement` | ✅      |
| `__VUE_*__` define flag injection                         | ✅      |
| `<style lang="scss">` etc. handed off to CSS preprocessor | ✅      |
| Custom blocks (`<i18n>`, …) virtual modules               | ✅      |
| Descriptor cache for HMR decisions                        | ✅ foundation; current fallback is full SFC reload |
| Granular HMR (template-only / style-only)                 | Gated on Farm/fervid hooks |
| Preprocessor re-scoping (scope id injected post-sass)     | Gated on Farm post-preprocessor hook ordering |
| `inlineTemplate: false` / external template split         | Gated on fervid per-block template codegen |
| Type-only `defineProps<…>()` cross-file deps              | Gated on fervid type dependency metadata |
| `componentIdGenerator`                                    | Gated on fervid configurable id support |
| `<script src>` / `<template src>` external blocks         | Experimental; verify against fervid before relying on it |
| Custom `compiler` (pin `vue/compiler-sfc` version)        | Dropped — fervid is the compiler |

## Comparison to `unplugin-vue` / `@vitejs/plugin-vue`

`@farmfe/plugin-vue` ports the bundler-facing behaviour of `unplugin-vue`'s Farm hooks (define flag injection, virtual style modules, custom-element filter) to Rust while delegating actual SFC compilation to `fervid` instead of `vue/compiler-sfc`. Most options carry over with the same names; the table above lists the ones that intentionally do not.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-wasm

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/wasm.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-wasm

A Rust Farm plugin for seamless WebAssembly integration, including support for `wasm-pack` generated modules.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install -D @farmfe/plugin-wasm</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add -D @farmfe/plugin-wasm</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add -D @farmfe/plugin-wasm</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import wasm from "@farmfe/plugin-wasm";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [wasm()],
});
```

Pre-compiled `.wasm` files can be imported with the `?init` query. The default export is an initialization function:

```ts
import init from "./example.wasm?init";

init().then((instance) => {
  instance.exports.test();
});
```

The initialization function can receive a WebAssembly import object:

```ts
import init from "./example.wasm?init";

init({
  imports: {
    someFunc: () => {},
  },
});
```

WASM packages can also be imported as ESM modules:

```ts
import { someFunc } from "wasm-project";

someFunc();
```

## Options

This plugin does not expose user options.

---

# @farmfe/plugin-worker

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/official-plugins/worker.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";

# @farmfe/plugin-worker

A Rust Farm plugin for importing web worker scripts with `new Worker()`, `new SharedWorker()`, and worker query suffixes.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install -D @farmfe/plugin-worker</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add -D @farmfe/plugin-worker</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add -D @farmfe/plugin-worker</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

Register the plugin in `farm.config.ts`:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import worker from "@farmfe/plugin-worker";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [worker()],
});
```

## Import via constructor

Use the standard worker constructor syntax:

```ts
const worker = new Worker(new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url));
```

Module workers are supported through the constructor options:

```ts
const worker = new Worker(new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url), {
  type: "module",
});
```

## Import with query suffix

Use `?worker` or `?sharedworker` to import a custom worker constructor:

```ts
import MyWorker from "./worker?worker";

const worker = new MyWorker();
```

Add `inline` to inline the worker as a base64 string, or `url` to read it as a URL:

```ts
import InlineWorker from "./worker?worker&inline";
import WorkerUrl from "./worker?worker&url";
```

## Options

- `compilerConfig?: Config` — optional Farm compilation config used when compiling workers.

# @farmfe/plugin-yaml

Inspired By [@rollup/plugin-yaml](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rollup/plugin-yaml)

🍣 A Farm plugin which Converts YAML files to ES6 modules.

## Installation

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
    <CodeBlock>npm install @farmfe/plugin-yaml</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
    <CodeBlock>yarn add @farmfe/plugin-yaml</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
    <CodeBlock>pnpm add @farmfe/plugin-yaml</CodeBlock>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Usage

farm.config.ts

```typescript
import { defineConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import yaml from '@farmfe/plugin-yaml';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    yaml({
      documentMode: 'single' | 'multi', // default single
      include: Regex, // default None,
      exclude: Regex, // default None
    }),
  ],
});
```

notice:

include or exclude is Regex not glob For example `**/01.yaml` is not illegal。What is right is like `".*\\/01.yaml"`

# Writing JavaScript Plugins

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/writing-plugins/js-plugin.mdx

import CodeBlock from "@theme/CodeBlock";
import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";


# Writing JavaScript Plugins

A JavaScript plugin is simply a pure JavaScript object that defines a set of property hooks:

```js
// farm.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";

export default defineConfig({
  // ...
  plugins: [
    // a plugin object
    {
      name: "my-resolve-plugin",
      priority: 1000, // the priority of this plugin, the larger the value, the earlier the execution. Normally internal plugins is 100.
      resolve: {
        filters: {
          // Only execute the hook when following conditions satisfied
          sources: ["\\./index.ts"], // a regex array
          importers: ["None"],
        },
        executor: async (param) => {
          // this hook executor
          console.log(param); // resolve params
          // return the resolve result
          return {
            resolvedPath: "virtual:my-module",
            query: [],
            sideEffects: false,
            external: false,
          };
        },
      },
    },
    // load, transform are similar to resolve, refer to their types
  ],
});
```

If you want to pass args to your plugins，you can use a closure.

```ts
// my-resolve-plugin.ts
export function myResolvePlugin(options: Options) {
  const { xx } = options;

  return {
    name: "my-resolve-plugin",
    resolve: {
      // ...
    },
  };
}

// farm.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "@farmfe/core";
import { myResolvePlugin } from "./myResolvePlugin.ts";

export default defineConfig({
  // ...
  plugins: [myResolvePlugin({ xx: "xx" })],
});
```

:::note
* See [Create Plugin](#create-plugin) to create a new plugin quickly based on official plugin templates.
* This document only covers how to create, develop and publish a js plugin, for more detail about the plugin hooks, see [Js Plugin Hooks](/docs/api/js-plugin-api).
:::

## Available Hooks (v2)

The following hooks are available in Farm v2's `JsPlugin` interface. See [Js Plugin API](/docs/api/js-plugin-api) for full details on each hook.

**Config & Server Hooks:**
- `config` — Modify the resolved config before compilation
- `configResolved` — Called after the config is fully resolved
- `configureServer` — Configure the dev server (add middlewares, etc.)
- `configureCompiler` — Access and configure the compiler instance

**Build Hooks:**
- `buildStart` — Called when the build starts
- `resolve` — Custom module resolution
- `load` — Custom module loading
- `transform` — Transform module content
- `processModule` — Process a module after transformation
- `freezeModule` — Called after a module is frozen (finalized during build)
- `buildEnd` — Called when the build ends

**Generate Hooks:**
- `renderStart` — Called when resource generation starts
- `processRenderedResourcePot` — Process a resource pot after rendering
- `augmentResourcePotHash` — Augment the hash of a resource pot. This is the TypeScript authoring name; the lower-level bridge still uses the historical `augmentResourceHash` name internally.
- `finalizeResources` — Finalize all resources before output
- `transformHtml` — Transform the generated HTML
- `writeResources` — Called when resources are written to disk

**Cache Hooks:**
- `pluginCacheLoaded` — Called when the plugin cache is loaded from disk
- `writePluginCache` — Called when the plugin cache is written to disk

**Lifecycle Hooks:**
- `finish` — Called when the compilation is finished
- `updateModules` — Called during HMR to determine which modules to update
- `updateFinished` — Called when HMR update is finished

## Conventions

For farm specific js plugins:

- The Farm Js plugin should have a name with a `farm-plugin-` prefix and clear semantics.
- Include the `farm-plugin-` keyword in package.json.

If your plugin is only applicable to a specific framework, its name should follow the following prefix format:

- `farm-plugin-vue-`: Prefix as a Vue plugin
- `farm-plugin-react-`: Prefix as a React plugin
- `farm-plugin-svelte-`: Prefix as a svelte plugin
- ...

## Concepts
Before you start to write your js plugin, you should know the following concepts:
* **filters**: Cause Js Plugins are much slower than Rust Plugins, your js plugin need to set explicit filters to avoid unnecessary call for js plugins hook. For example, you should set `transform.filters.moduleTypes = ['js']` to make sure that the transform hook of your js plugin only runs for `.js/mjs/cjs` files.
* **module_type**: The type of the module, it can be `js`, `ts`, `css`, `sass`, `json`, etc. Farm supports `js/ts/jsx/tsx`, `css`, `html`, `json`, `static assets(png, svg, etc)` natively. `module_type` is returned by `load` hook or `transform` hook.
* **resolved_path and module_id**: `resolved_path` is the absolute path of the module, and `module_id` is the unique id of the module, it's usually `relative path of the module from the project root` + `query`. For example, we import a module as `import './a?query'`, the resolved_path is `/project/src/a.ts` and the module_id is `src/a.ts?query`.
* **context**: All the hooks in the plugin accept a `context` argument, it's the compilation context of the farm project, you can use it to get the ModuleGraph, Module, Resources, etc.
* **Resource and Resource Pot**: `Resource` is the final output bundle file, and `Resource Pot` is the abstract representation of the resource, similar to `Chunk` of other bundlers. Inside Farm, first we will generate `Resource Pots` from `ModuleGraph`, render `Resource Pots` and finally generate `Resources` from `Resource Pots`.

### Filters
Cause `Js Plugins` are much slower than `Rust Plugins`, Farm use `filters` to control the execution of js plugin hooks. The plugin hook executes only when given `filters` matched to improve performance. `filters` is necessary for some commonly used hooks, such as `resolve`, `load`, `transform`, etc. 

For example, if you want to transform css files, you can use `transform.filters.moduleTypes = ['css']` to make sure that the transform hook of your js plugin only runs for `.css` files:

```ts
const myCssPlugin = {
  name: "my-css-plugin",
  transform: {
    filters: {
      // Only execute the hook when following conditions satisfied
      // resolvedPaths: ["\\./index.ts"], // a regex array to match the resolvedPaths
      moduleTypes: ["css"],
    },
    executor: async (param) => {
      // transform css
    },
  },
};
```

### Module Type
In Farm, every thing is `First Class Citizens`, so Farm designs `module_type` to identify the type of a module and handle different kinds of ModuleTypes in different plugins. 

`module_type` returned by `load` hook, and can be transformed by `transform` hook. Farm supports `js/ts/jsx/tsx`, `css`, `html`, `json`, `static assets(png, svg, etc)` natively. For these module types, you can return them directly in `load` or `transform` hook directly. JavaScript plugins can use `processModule` and `freezeModule` for later module-level processing, but custom parsing, rendering, and resource generation hooks are Rust-only.

:::note
Js Plugins don't support `parse`, `render_resource_pot`, `generate_resources` hooks, you have to use Rust Plugins to handle custom module types.
::: 

## Create Plugin
Farm provides official templates to help your create your js plugins quickly:
<>
    <Tabs>
      <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
          <CodeBlock>pnpm create farm-plugin</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>
          <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
              <CodeBlock>npm create farm-plugin@latest</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
          <CodeBlock>yarn create farm-plugin</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>
          </Tabs>
</>

then follow the prompts to create your plugin.

or you can create a plugin directly by running the following command:
<Tabs>
      <TabItem value="pnpm" label="pnpm">
          <CodeBlock>pnpm create farm-plugin my-farm-plugin --type js</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>
          <TabItem value="npm" label="npm">
              <CodeBlock>npm create farm-plugin@latest my-farm-plugin -- --type js</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="yarn" label="yarn">
          <CodeBlock>yarn create farm-plugin my-farm-plugin --type js</CodeBlock>
              </TabItem>
          </Tabs>
Above command will create new js plugin with name `my-farm-plugin` in the current directory. `--type` can be `rust` or `js`

## Develop Plugin
After creating the plugin, you can start to develop your plugin. The plugin is a pure JavaScript object that defines a set of property hooks:

```ts
// import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import type { JsPlugin } from '@farmfe/core';

interface Options {
  /* Your options here */
}

export default function farmPlugin(options: Options): JsPlugin {
  return {
    name: '<FARM-JS-PLUGIN-NPM-NAME>',
    /* Your plugin hooks here: */ 

    // transform: {
    //   filters: {
    //     moduleTypes: ['js']
    //   },
    //   async executor(params) {
    //     const { content } = params;
    //     return {
    //       content,
    //       moduleType: 'js'
    //     };
    //   }
    // },
    // finish: {
    //   executor() {}
    // }
  };
}
```

:::tip
For more detail about the plugin hooks, see [Js Plugin Hooks](/docs/api/js-plugin-api).
:::

Run `npm run dev` to compile the plugin and watch for changes. Run `npm run build` to build the plugin.

## Publish Plugin
A js plugin package is a normal npm package, you can publish it to npm registry by running `npm publish`.

# Overview

Source: https://github.com/farm-fe/farm/blob/main/website/docs/plugins/writing-plugins/overview.md


# Overview
To use a Rust plugin, configuring `plugins` in `farm.config.ts`.

```ts
import { defineFarmConfig } from '@farmfe/core';
import react from '@farmfe/plugin-react';

defineFarmConfig({
  // ...
  plugins: [
    { /*..*/ }, // Js plugin, a object with hook defined
    react(), // rust plugin imported and called like a JS plugin
  ]
})

```

Farm support both rust plugins and js plugins:

* [Writing Rust Plugin](/docs/plugins/writing-plugins/rust-plugin)
* [Writing Js Plugin](/docs/plugins/writing-plugins/js-plugin)
<!-- * [Writing Runtime Plugin](/docs/plugins/writing-plugins/runtime-plugin) -->
